identification.summary: Xiaoqiying (also Genesis Day, Teng Snake) is a primarily Chinese-speaking hacktivist group that Recorded Future's Insikt Group assessed as motivated mainly by patriotism toward China, based on its Telegram channels, special-access forum posts and a clearnet website [S1][S2]. It is best known for defacing 12 South Korean research and academic websites during the Lunar New Year holiday in late January 2023 [S1][S3]. S2W's earlier profile of 'Teng Snake (a.k.a. Code Core)' says the group began running Telegram channels and group chats in October 2021 and had four core members and seven sub-teams [S4].
identification.firstObserved: 2021-10 (S2W reports the group's Telegram channels and group chats began in October 2021) [S4]
identification.notes: S2W reports Teng Snake claimed the designation APT-C-61 [S4]. A Heimdal write-up of the January 2023 Samsung claim describes 'Genesis Day' as pro-Russian, which conflicts with Insikt's Chinese-language, pro-China assessment [S1][S6]; the encyclopedia record treats Insikt's assessment as the better-sourced one but the conflict is unresolved. The mapping of Teng Snake/Code Core (S2W, 2022) to Xiaoqiying/Genesis Day (Insikt, 2023) is stated by Insikt-aligned secondary sources and Malpedia but I could not open the primary documents to confirm the basis.

attribution.sponsor: No state sponsor established. Insikt found no clear ties to the Chinese government and assessed the group as a hacktivist actor [S1][S2].
attribution.confidence: Insikt's assessment is hacktivist motivation (patriotism toward China) with no clear government tie; a German-language version of the Insikt report rates the credibility of the group's claims as medium [S1]. This is a vendor assessment, not a government attribution.
attribution.basis: Insikt analyzed the group's Telegram channels, special-access forum postings and clearnet website [S1]. KISA traced IP addresses linked to the January 2023 attack to China, the US, Singapore and Taiwan, which does not by itself establish origin [S3].

objectives: Pro-China patriotic hacktivism: the group vowed to target NATO countries and any country or region deemed hostile to China [S1]. It said KISA was its intended first government target in South Korea [S3]. In a January 2023 claim against Samsung the group cited South Korea's opening of a NATO mission [S5].

targeting.notes: Confirmed: 12 South Korean research and academic sites defaced, including departments of Jeju University and the Korea National University of Education [S3]. Claimed and unverified: theft of 54 GB of data, a threat against about 2,000 South Korean government agencies [S2][S3], and intrusion into Samsung Group's internal FTP, employee system and intranet, which Samsung said it was verifying [S5]. Insikt reported that affiliated actors signaled new attacks on organizations in Japan and Taiwan [S1]; forum posts also made unverified claims of compromising organizations in the US, Ukraine, Taiwan, South Korea and Japan [S1].

capabilities.summary: The observed effect was website defacement: attackers replaced each hosted website with their own content on a compromised server [S3]. The group released penetration-testing tools, malware, proofs of concept and exploits and disclosed data, and claimed to work with known cybercriminal and APT groups (claim, unverified) [S1]. Malpedia lists no malware families associated with the actor [S1]. Insikt's credibility rating for its claims was medium [S1].

campaigns.name: Telegram channels and group chats begin
campaigns.summary: S2W reports the Teng Snake group began running Telegram channels and group chats in October 2021 [S4].

campaigns.name: Samsung internal systems claim
campaigns.summary: Calling itself Genesis Day, the group claimed access to Samsung Group's internal FTP service, employee system and intranet, citing South Korea's opening of a NATO mission; Samsung said it was verifying the claim [S5]. Reporting on the leak's sensitivity varied and sample data reviewed by Cybernews appeared to hold little sensitive content [S6]. Samsung's breach was not confirmed in the sources reviewed.

campaigns.name: South Korean academic and research site defacements
campaigns.summary: During the Lunar New Year holiday in late January 2023 the group defaced 12 South Korean research and academic websites; KISA reported the sites were replaced with attacker content on a compromised server [S1][S3]. The group said KISA was its intended first government target and claimed 54 GB of stolen data (unverified) [S2][S3].

campaigns.name: Telegram channels shut down
campaigns.summary: The group's two Telegram channels (an announcement channel and a members channel under the 'Genesis Day' moniker) went offline in early February 2023 after media coverage of the South Korea attacks [S1][S2].

campaigns.name: Signals of Japan and Taiwan attacks
campaigns.summary: Insikt reported on 2023-04-20 that affiliated actors had signaled a new round of attacks on organizations in Japan and Taiwan [S1][S2].

diamond.adversary: Primarily Chinese-speaking, pro-China hacktivist collective; S2W describes four core members and seven sub-teams [S1][S4]. No known government tie [S1].
diamond.capability: Website defacement, claimed data theft, and release or use of public tools, exploits and malware; no unique malware family documented [S1][S3].
diamond.infrastructure: Telegram announcement and members channels, special-access forum accounts and a clearnet website [S1]. Attack IPs traced by KISA to China, the US, Singapore and Taiwan [S3]. Specific domains and IPs not obtained.
diamond.victim: South Korean research and academic institutions; claimed Samsung and government agencies; signaled Japan and Taiwan targets [S1][S3][S5].
diamond.socioPolitical: Patriotic opposition to NATO engagement in East Asia and to countries seen as hostile to China, expressed around South Korea's NATO mission opening [S1][S5].
diamond.technology: Web hosting servers of academic sites (compromised server used for defacement); exact initial access vector not documented in the sources reviewed [S3].

gaps: Could not open the primary Insikt report, The Record articles or the S2W profile with WebFetch (host resolution failed); content relies on search-result summaries of those documents.
Initial access methods, exploited vulnerabilities and tooling for the 2023 defacements are not documented in the sources reviewed.
The 54 GB data theft, the 2,000 government agency threat and the Samsung breach are unverified claims.
Heimdal's description of Genesis Day as pro-Russian conflicts with Insikt's pro-China assessment; unresolved.

Link between S2W's Teng Snake/Code Core profile (2022) and Insikt's Xiaoqiying/Genesis Day (2023) not verified from primary text; S2W profile is dated 2022-07-07 and APT-C-61 is a separate South Asia-focused cluster in HivePro reporting, so the APT-C-61 claim is unreliable.
No activity after April 2023 was found; whether the group is dormant, rebranded or active is unknown.
Actual Japan and Taiwan attacks following the April 2023 signaling were not verified.
MITRE ATT&CK group ID: none in the existing record.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Step 1-2: the operational environment is East Asian academic, research and corporate web infrastructure in South Korea, Taiwan and Japan, with US-allied networks as stated targets [S1][S3]. Step 3-4 (adversary): a pro-China hacktivist collective with no established state tie, using defacement and claimed data theft, with unverified claims inflated for effect [S1][S2]. MLCOA: opportunistic defacement and data-leak claims against weakly secured public-facing sites of Korean, Taiwanese and Japanese institutions, timed to political or holiday events [S1][S3]. MDCOA: the group or affiliates escalate to intrusions at larger corporate or government targets, as the Samsung and government-agency claims suggest, or act as an influence front for a state actor (no evidence either way) [S1][S5]. Candidate indicators: new Telegram channels using the Genesis Day or Teng Snake monikers, forum posts claiming East Asian victims, and defacement content on unpatched hosting servers [S1][S4].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: monitor hacktivist Telegram and forum claims against allied East Asian entities and treat unverified claims as low-confidence until victims confirm [S1][S5]. Authorities: this is a criminal and civil-defense problem for host-nation agencies such as KISA, so US support runs through partner-nation and law enforcement channels rather than military response [S3]. Mission assurance: the sourced activity targeted academic and public websites, not military systems, so direct mission impact is low, but defacements and leaks of allied corporate data can affect partner confidence and information environment [S1][S3]. Coordination: share indicators with ROK, Japanese and Taiwanese counterparts and with commercial threat intelligence providers who track the group [S1][S4].
